title: Holding Back Freshly Deposited Money from the Available Balance
content:
Money that has only just reached an account of Savings & Money Market Accounts is held back for owners carrying card debt. Two facts are read from the owner's card under Personal Credit Cards: the balance owed on it, and the unredeemed rewards points it carries. The figure held back is measured from the deposits posted to the savings account in the one calendar month ending on the instruction date.

**Where the card owes at least 2000.00 USD and carries fewer than 10000 unredeemed rewards points**, those deposits are held back from the available balance in full.

**Where the card owes at least 2000.00 USD and carries at least 10000 unredeemed rewards points**, half of those deposits is held back, that is 0.50 of their total, rounded to the cent.

**Where the card owes less than 2000.00 USD**, the available balance is the settled balance, with nothing held back.

### A worked case on hypothetical inputs

Take a savings account whose settled balance is 18000.00 USD and whose deposits in the one calendar month ending on the instruction date come to 3000.00 USD.

Where the owner's card owes 2500.00 USD and carries 4000 unredeemed points, the whole 3000.00 USD is held back and the available balance is 15000.00 USD. Where the card owes the same 2500.00 USD but carries 12000 unredeemed points, 1500.00 USD is held back and the available balance is 16500.00 USD. Where the card owes 900.00 USD, nothing is held back and the available balance is the settled balance of 18000.00 USD.

The held-back figure never takes the available balance below zero.

### Boundary figures

A card balance owed of exactly 2000.00 USD falls in one of the first two branches; 1999.99 USD falls in the third whatever the rewards points. Exactly 10000 unredeemed rewards points puts the account in the second branch rather than the first.
